name: stations-r3
note: Stations round 3 (owner, 2026-10-24): the Dairy from two new concepts (the big roof is not a good template for it, the cow sign felt tacked on), the Kitchen, and the Winery (open air, aspirational). The roof is not essential. Two candidates each.

dairy-c.prompt: STYLE, CAMERA AND SCALE REFERENCES: the first attached panel is this game's APPROVED MILL crafting station: match its painterly storybook rendering, its bright daylight, its camera (the front square to the viewer, seen a little from above, the grid straight), its scale (people-sized posts, two tiles wide) and its stall bones where they fit: an open-air cut-away workshop with a plank or stone back wall along the top edge, low side walls, NO front wall, the floor packed earth with flagstones, a lantern. A roof is NOT required: use one only if the concept wants it. PROP CAMERA: the second attached image is this game's barrel; every prop is drawn from that camera, mostly from the front and a little from above, tops as narrow ellipses. SUBJECT: the DAIRY, where milk becomes butter and cheese. CONCEPT C, THE CHEESE PRESS: no roof. A cool stone-flagged dairy yard with a low whitewashed stone back wall and side walls; the natural tall piece is a big wooden CHEESE PRESS at the back-left: a heavy timber frame with a tall screw and a crossbar, pressing a cheese in a round mould, rising above the wall; along the back wall a wooden rack of three big CHEESE WHEELS (one with a wedge cut); at the right a plain butter churn, a crate of glass milk bottles and a tin milk churn; wooden pails hanging on the side wall; a pat of butter on a stone slab. ACCENT: cream white stone with SKY-BLUE painted woodwork (the press frame, the rack, the pails). It must read as a dairy at a glance. The LAST attached image is a layout guide, a patch of the board grid with a tan 2 x 2 square: the station's walls, floor and pieces fill that 2 x 2 square entirely, back on its top edge, ground contact on its bottom edge, sides to its left and right edges (its tallest piece may rise above it), with a soft contact shadow to the lower right. Fill the surrounding squares with plain short grass in the same style, no props beyond those named, and draw the faint grid lines as thin tile edges. Do not leave the tan square tan. No letters anywhere, no people, no animals, no smoke, no steam.
